question.problem:
Let $f(x)$ be the $2\pi $-periodic extension of the function $F(x)=\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2}+3$ defined on $[-\pi ,\pi ).$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below, showing the derivation of the Fourier series of the $2\pi $-periodic extension of $G(x)=7x$ from the corresponding Fourier series of $f(x).$The Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2}+3∼3+\frac{7{\pi }^{2}}{6}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{14(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}}{{field-1}}.
$$

current_example.problem:
Let $f(x)$ be the $10$-periodic extension of the function
$F(x)=\dfrac{5}{2}x^2-3$
defined on $[-5,5).$ Fill in the blanks in the reasoning below, showing the derivation of the Fourier series of the $10$-periodic extension of $G(x)=5x$
from the corresponding Fourier series of $f(x).$

The Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

Since $f$ is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14229051/assets/5c0cbee364829774ec30c1d908574bc181363a8d2ce0acb705920f36b5057796.svg)

on $\mathbb{R},$ we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term to get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14229051/assets/c7d5e1b3dcd931bb3aef77696ddfa6c89063db234e03fff4904e022e1a2bc4ff.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
First, notice that $F(x)$ is an even function. So, the Fourier series of its $2L$-periodic extension has the form

$$
\dfrac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{L}\right).
$$

In our case, $L=5.$ Thus, the Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x) \sim \dfrac{107}{6}
+ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{250(-1)^n}{n^2\pi^2}
\bbox[4pt, border: solid 0.5pt black]{\cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{5}\right)}.
$$

Now, notice that  

- the function $F$ is continuously differentiable on $(-5,5),$

- continuous on $[-5,5),$ and

- satisfies $F(-5)=F(5),$ if we extend the value at $x=5$ using the formula $F(x)=\dfrac{5}{2}x^2-3.$

Therefore, the $10$-periodic extension $f$ is $\bbox[4pt, border: solid 0.5pt black]{\text{continuous} }$ and $\bbox[4pt, border: solid 0.5pt black]{\text{piecewise smooth}}$
on $\mathbb{R},$ so we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5}{2}{x}^{2}-3) & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{107}{6})+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{250(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{5})) \\ 5x & ∼0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{250(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\cdot (-\frac{n\pi }{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{5})) \\ 5x & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{-50(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{5}) \\ 5x & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{50(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{5}).\end{aligned}
$$
